pairs.question: Quid tam novum quam adulescentulum privatum exercitum difficili rei publicae temporare conficere?
pairs.derivation: Cicero poses a rhetorical question about Pompey's career and answers it himself with the single perfect verb 'Confecit.' Boundaries are the full question sentence (ending at the '?') and its one-word answer (to the full stop). Nothing cut. The section marker [61] is stripped. 'temporare' kept verbatim as it stands in the source (apparent edition typo for 'tempore').

pairs.question: Huic praeesse?
pairs.derivation: Immediately follows the 'Confecit' exchange; Cicero again poses a clipped question ('To command it?') and answers it himself ('He did command'). 'Huic' refers to the just-mentioned exercitum, intelligible from the preceding pair. Question ends at '?', answer at the full stop. Nothing cut.

pairs.question: Rem optime ductu suo gerere?
pairs.derivation: Third in the question/self-answer series in this section; Cicero asks ('To wage the campaign excellently under his own leadership?') and answers ('He waged it'). Question ends at '?', answer is the single perfect verb to the full stop. Nothing cut.

pairs.question: Quid tam inusitatum quam ut, cum duo consules clarissimi fortissimique essent, eques Romanus ad bellum maximum formidolosissimumque pro consule mitteretur?
pairs.derivation: Cicero poses the question of whether it was unheard-of for a Roman knight to be sent as proconsul, then answers himself with 'Missus est.' Boundaries: full question sentence to the '?', answer to the full stop. Section marker [62] stripped. Nothing internal cut.
